evidence: M-O s.v. speak: do you speak Latin?
terms.comment: The adverb names the language; for modern ones see in English, in Bulgarian, in Portuguese. Lewis & Short notes that Latīnē loquī can also mean to speak good, plain Latin (Cic. Brut. 166).

evidence: Cic. Brut. 140: nōn enim tam praeclārum est scīre Latīnē quam turpe nescīre

phrases.latin: nōn tamen hoc adeō superstitiōsē fierī velim, ut diū tantum Graecē loquātur aut discat, sīcut plērīsque mōris est
phrases.english: But I would not have this done so rigidly that he speaks or learns only Greek for a long time, as most people do.

phrases.latin: nōn enim tam praeclārum est scīre Latīnē quam turpe nescīre
phrases.english: For knowing Latin is not so much a credit as not knowing it is a disgrace.

phrases.latin: scīs enim mē Graecē loquī in Latīnō sermōne nōn plūs solēre quam in Graecō Latīnē
phrases.english: For you know I am no more in the habit of speaking Greek in a Latin conversation than Latin in a Greek one.
